While aged human T cells retain their capacity to migrate ex vivo, they exhibit impaired cellular deformability and deficiencies in sensing local biological signals. To modulate this surveillance defect, we perform mechanical reprogramming using elevated fluid viscosity. Results indicate that acute priming of aged T cells with elevated fluid viscosity recovers a transient young-like surveillance phenotype, particularly within CD4 + memory T cell populations. This recovered young-like phenotype is mechanistically linked to elevated SDF-1α receptor expression together with increased membrane tension, cortical F-actin, and Arp3 expression. Altogether, these findings identify a key source of surveillance defects among aged T cells and offer an effective mechano-inducible strategy for modulating single-cell behaviors.

papers.title: Spatial targeting and expansion prevention offer effective pathways to protect African maize from parasitic weeds.
papers.authors: Tonle FBN, Segnon AC, Gouroubera MW, Makumbi D, De Groote H, Niassy S, Chagomoka T, Tonnang H, Zougmore RB.
papers.abstract: Parasitic weeds (Striga spp.) threaten food security for over 300 million Africans dependent on maize, yet economic impact estimates vary widely due to high uncertainties, limiting strategic planning and interventions. We developed a spatially-explicit framework overcoming data scarcity through integrated agroecological similarity mapping, machine learning, and stochastic modeling to quantify Striga economic impacts across African maize production systems. Our analysis resolves decades of uncertainty, revealing annual losses of US$1.04 billion (95% confidence interval: US$0.94-1.15 billion) with high spatial concentration: less than 6% of infested areas generate half the economic losses. Agricultural expansion represents the primary future risk, potentially tripling losses by 2050 as Striga colonizes new areas. Interventions achieve maximum impact through a dual strategy: spatial targeting of high-loss zones coupled with prevention in agricultural expansion areas. This targeted approach outperforms uniform intensification, providing a blueprint for managing agricultural pests in data-scarce regions.

papers.title: Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models.
papers.authors: Yao M, Pan Y, Zhong Y, Mei S, Qin Z, Wang K, Hu J, Ding S, Hu T, Huang Y, Xu S, Deng L, Zheng Z, Huang M, Shen X, Xu NL, Hu Y, Chou Y, Zhou P, Sun G, Qiao N, Yan J, Xu B, Li G.
papers.abstract: A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor. We challenge this perspective by establishing a biological analogy between simplified dendritic neuron models and the attention mechanisms central to AI foundation models. We show that AI attention mechanisms bear direct mappings to internal neuronal complexities arising from dendritic organization, rather than to the mere inter-neuronal connections of simple point neurons. This re-conceptualization not only offers a neuroscience-informed perspective for understanding core AI methodologies beyond their formulation as abstract mathematical operations, but also paves the way for neuro-inspired foundation models that leverage neuroscientific insights to sustainably advance modern AI beyond scaling laws. As an example of this paradigm, we introduce a dendritic-inspired complexity framework, and design a hybrid-attention foundation model with dendritic-inspired sparse computation, which enhances memory capacity while reducing computational demands. Our model supports a 50M context window-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare-demonstrating superior long-term memory capabilities. This work pioneers a paradigm that harnesses intra-neuronal dynamics to drive sustained advances in modern AI, while also offering a potential route to understanding dendritic computational mechanisms.

papers.title: Brain-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies.
papers.authors: Oz Rokach R, Marmor O, Levy Y, Gilad A.
papers.abstract: It is long thought that higher-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location (i.e., 'what' and 'where' streams). Here, using the mouse whisker system, we demonstrate an existence of two alternating brain-wide (beyond cortex) subnetworks that are primarily driven by internal strategies, rather than external parameters. We combine simultaneous brain-wide neuronal recordings in male mice trained to identify or locate a certain stimulus. We find that mice deploy either an active search or a passive sensation strategy during task performance. These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively. Using a computational framework, we show that the posterior subnetwork encoded additional internal strategic parameters such as trial history, the first task of the day, and training history. When discarding the dominance of the frontal subnetwork, specific areas within the posterior subnetwork encoded meaningful task information regarding object identity and location. Integrated together, these two subnetworks may comprise optimal sensory integration.

papers.title: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps.
papers.authors: Perez L, Shi L, Daspit A, Pruett KN, Smith C, Prideaux A, Sousa JF, Schneider PN.
papers.abstract: The emergence of evolutionary novelties remains a central challenge in biology, particularly for complex organs such as the vertebrate eye. Here, we use the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps to investigate adaptation to simultaneous aerial and aquatic vision. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal that the ventral retina, which processes aerial light, is developmentally expanded and exhibits region-specific opsin expression. Ventral PR1 cones express opn1mw2 rather than the longer-wavelength-sensitive opn1lw paralogs expressed dorsally. Machine-learning predictions indicate that Opn1mw2 is red-shifted relative to Opn1mw1 but remains blue-shifted relative to dorsal Opn1lw pigments. Dorsal-ventral patterning markers further reveal an overrepresentation of ventral retinal identities. Comparative spatial profiling of developing and adult Anableps and killifish indicates dorsal displacement of the retinal boundary, producing a proportionally larger ventral domain. Thus, Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of the ventral retina and regional reconfiguration of opsin expression within conserved cone subtypes.

papers.title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts.
papers.authors: O'Ferrall AM, Lally D, Makaula P, Namacha G, Lewis JM, Musicha P, Goodman RN, Allman E, Moyo SJ, Waddington CS, Kayuni SA, Feasey NA, Musaya J, Stothard JR, Roberts AP.
papers.abstract: Infection with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-Ec) is a global health concern that disproportionately affects sub-Saharan Africa. Gut mucosal colonisation is thought to precede invasive infection. Understanding ESBL-Ec colonisation and transmission across communities is therefore essential. Here, we investigate the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of 159 gut-colonising ESBL-Ec isolates from the faeces of 211 people in two rural Malawian villages using longitudinal sampling (2023-24), whole-genome sequencing and household mapping. Colonisation prevalence rose from 34.1% (95% CI: 27.8-41.0) to 54.2% (95% CI: 46.0-62.3) over one year. Isolates belonged to 33 sequence types (STs), most commonly ST38 and ST131, harbouring 46 distinct antimicrobial resistance gene types. Fifteen strains were identified in ≥3 households that were typically separated by short geographic distances ( < 400 m). Of 190 pairwise comparisons between same-strain isolates from different households sampled concurrently within villages, 88.9% differed by ≤10 single nucleotide polymorphisms, consistent with multi-household involvement in community transmission networks. Lineage-specific ST38 and ST131 network analyses linked rural isolates to urban Malawian isolates collected within the last decade. Our findings provide a transferable framework for inferring ESBL-Ec flow in community settings and highlight the need for One Health surveillance and improved sanitation infrastructure to limit transmission.

papers.title: Genotype-phenotype single-cell transcriptomics for massive parallel assessment of genetic variants.
papers.authors: Vaccaro L, De Santis R, Panariello F, Grimaldi A, Gandolfo G, Massa M, Fusco T, Salvi M, Capuana R, Riccardo S, Annunziata P, Colantuono C, Martone G, Bamundo M, Xanthopoulou EM, Schertler L, Damon C, Gambardella G, Arnese R, Agolini E, Cesario C, Abdelrazek IM, AbdelGhany H, Novelli A, Salvatori B, Cesana M, Ziegenhain C, Missero C, Cacchiarelli D.
papers.abstract: Predicting the pathogenic effect of rare genetic variants is significantly hampered by the limited cohort of diagnosed patients and the difficulty in functionally evaluating the effect of existing and novel variants. To address this issue, we leveraged a protein Multiplexed Assay of Variants Effect (MAVE) to functionally assess the effect of ~ 2200 missense variants of the TP63 gene, some of which cause autosomal dominant developmental disorders. The activity of each variant was measured using an optimized fibroblast-to-keratinocyte conversion protocol, and a subset of mutants was validated through multiple orthogonal biochemical and genomics functional assays to assess consistency and robustness. To systematically expand MAVEs beyond predefined assay, we here introduce SCRAMseq (Single Cell RNAseq Associated with MAVEs by sequencing). This generalizable platform leverages full-length scRNAseq for high-throughput, single-cell genotype-to-phenotype mapping. We validate SCRAMseq across different experimental and genetic contexts to demonstrate its reproducibility and accuracy. SCRAMseq provides a robust and versatile workflow poised to accelerate the discovery and dissection of gene variant effects on any potential disease-driving pathway, thereby significantly broadening MAVEs applicability to virtually any possible disease-driving gene.

papers.title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis.
papers.authors: Liu L, Zhu L, Monteiro-Martins S, Griffin A, Vlahos LJ, Fujita M, Taylor AD, Berrouet C, Zanoni F, Marasa M, Zhang JY, Zhou XJ, Caliskan Y, Akchurin O, Al-Akash S, Jankauskiene A, Bodria M, Chishti A, Esposito C, Esposito V, Claes D, Tesar V, Davis TK, Samsonov D, Kaminska D, Hryszko T, Zaza G, Flynn JT, Iorember F, Lugani F, Rizk D, Julian BA, Hidalgo G, Kallash M, Biancone L, Amoroso A, Bono L, Mani LY, Vogt B, Lin F, Sreedharan R, Weng P, Ranch D, Xiao N, Quiroga A, Matar RB, Rheault MN, Wenderfer S, Selewski D, Lundberg S, Silva C, Mason S, Mahan JD, Vasylyeva TL, Mucha K, Foroncewicz B, Pączek L, Florczak M, Olszewska M, Gradzińska A, Szczepańska M, Machura E, Badeński A, Krakowczyk H, Sikora P, Kwella N, Miklaszewska M, Drożdż D, Zaniew M, Pawlaczyk K, Siniewicz-Luzeńczyk K, Bomback AS, Appel GB, Izzi C, Scolari F, Materna-Kiryluk A, Mizerska-Wasiak M, Berthelot L, Pillebout E, Monteiro RC, Hall S, Qiu S, Shang Q, Reily C, Novak J, Green TJ, Smoyer WE, Colleen Hastings M, Wyatt RJ, Nelson R, Khan A, Martin J, González-Gay MA, De Jager PL, Köttgen A, Califano A, Gharavi AG, Zhang H, Kiryluk K.
papers.abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10 -25 ) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10 -20 ), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10 -09 ), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells.

papers.title: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors.
papers.authors: Puig-I-Laborda V, Carrasco Muriel J, Castañeda Tena A, Groves T, le Nepvou de Carfort J, Krühne U, Gernaey KV, Haringa C, Puig-de-Dou I, Nielsen LK.
papers.abstract: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on 760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test R2≈0.91 ), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference-up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

papers.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism.
papers.authors: Teng H, Yu H, Xu Z, Xiao L, Yuan X, Yang L, Wu J, Xu G.
papers.abstract: Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. (R)-3-([1,1'-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis.

papers.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes.
papers.authors: Wen Y, Schlegel HH, Fox D, Wang C, Harutyunyan A, Gao R, Gao W, Zhang Q, Khanna P, Arias AC.
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode-skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

papers.title: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing.
papers.authors: Cumer T, Topaloudis A, Lavanchy E, Ducrest AL, Sarmiento Cabello S, Hewett A, Becciu P, Simon C, Marquis J, Charpagne A, Almasi B, Roulin A, Goudet J.
papers.abstract: Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls (Tyto alba) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

papers.title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Ren Y, Kong D, Feng J, Hu K, Xu X, Deng F, Li P, Wang J, Huang W, Wei G, Su Y, Tan Y, Zhang S, Sun X, Kang F, Yan H.
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery.

papers.title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases.
papers.authors: Li M, Tatar A, Green E, Simsek E, Kahraman CY, Ceylan M, Laloglu F, Ceviz N, Tatar A, Laloglu E, Akcay G, Cadirci K, Yapca OE, Ozmen HK, Yapanoglu T, Kudas O, Simsek F, Yılmaz EPT, Senocak GNC, Doneray H, Ozden A, Cayir A, Tasar PT, Kara M, Aktaş YE, Karadavut M, Akpinar B, Calik ES, Erkut B, Akcay M, Karadeniz E, Kartal M, Disci E, Yildirgan MI, Atamanalp SS, Peksoz R, Albayrak Y, Eroglu A, Aydın Y, Gur STA, Gul M, Tekin E, Ulas AB, Senocak E, Paksoy AE, Donmez AS, Turgut MC, Ozmen O, Alper F, Guliyev HA, Albayrak B, Cinici E, Kocer I, Aydın EF, Dogan N, Gul Y, Kaya U, Topdagi YE, Kumtepe Y, Dostbil A, Kursat H, Bilge N, Cinici O, Disci E, Cevizli D, Guler MA, Ozcan H, Koca Lacin T, Sari S, Kerget B, Araz O, Tortum F, Altundas N, Aksungur N, Kara S, Ozturk G, Kaya SK, Ulku M, Can FK, Alay H, Albayrak A, Ozden K, Karatas E, Ozen MM, Gur A, Arabaci T, Yilar S, Saritas S, Ozkurt Z, Ceyhun HA, Sevinc C, Sirin MA, Sincan G, Kanjee M, Saruhan B, Eren SO, Utlu B, Tas MH, Tanriverdi E, Álvez MB, Edfors F, Kong X, Song X, Altay O, Yuksel B, Uhlen M, Shoaie S, Zhang C, Turkez H, Mardinoglu A.
papers.abstract: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition-specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA-protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

papers.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Xu X, Chen X, Zhang Y, Zheng W, Zhang T.
papers.abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG-mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG-eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied to 11,976 sewage-derived SAGs. This approach yielded 4,198 SAGs passing Scellmate's whole-SAG curation, which captured pronounced heterogeneity masked by bulk methods. At the species level, we resolved extensive hidden diversity within abundant taxa such as Aliarcobacter that was unresolved by matched metagenome-assembled genomes; at the strain level, we pinpointed a distinct Agathobacter rectalis cluster carrying specialized carbon-utilization pathways, suggesting niche differentiation. Leveraging these curated SAGs, we identified 6,474 host-mobilome linkages across 2,378 SAGs; these linkages not only showed high concordance with host-association data within the Integrated Microbial Genomes (IMG) system but also significantly expanded species-level host assignments. Furthermore, we detected frequent inter-species sharing patterns of diverse cryptic plasmids within the order Bacteroidales. Together, this work demonstrates that high-throughput single-cell genomics, empowered by the robust framework, resolves fine-scale heterogeneity and host-mobilome dynamics, advancing culture-independent microbiome research.

papers.title: Microbial ecological instability and non-linear host interactions shape airway inflammation in HIV-associated COPD.
papers.authors: Kayongo A, Bartolomaeus TUP, Hecker J, Birkner T, Vila E, Ntayi ML, Markó L, Löber U, Olweny G, Kyalo E, Kyamulabi D, Ndawula J, Ssengooba W, Nabatanzi R, Kyobe S, Nassali F, Kigozi E, Kalyesubula R, Munana R, Namaganda J, Musiime CJ, Sekibira R, Bagaya BS, Kateete DP, Joloba ML, Jjingo D, Lusiba J, Worodria W, Mayanja-Kizza H, Lalitha R, Ham W, Sanyu I, Zawedde J, Robertson NM, Obondo JS, Weidinger C, Kunkel D, Kirenga BJ, Siddharthan T, Hurst JR, Checkley W, Cookson WB, Moffatt MF, Forslund-Startceva SK.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized among people living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, yet the mechanisms linking airway microbial ecology to chronic inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we study 200 adults stratified by HIV and COPD status, including 160 participants with two-year longitudinal follow-up, using an integrated multi-omics framework combining sputum 16S rRNA profiling, bacterial outer membrane vesicle quantification, airway cytokine profiling, CyTOF immune phenotyping, bulk transcriptomics of induced sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage and peripheral blood, and bronchoalveolar lavage single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution. We find that sputum microbial communities are shaped predominantly by temporal ecological turnover rather than HIV or COPD status. Although microbial diversity, microbiome instability, outer membrane vesicle burden and inferred airway cellular composition remain largely preserved, HIV-associated COPD exhibits disease-specific microbial signatures together with inflammatory transcriptional remodeling concentrated in induced sputum. Integrated analyses identify selective host-microbe interaction networks linking discrete microbial taxa with inflammatory, immune and transcriptional programmes.

papers.title: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms.
papers.authors: Selvaraj J, Cheng J.
papers.abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. However, several inherent limitations in cryo-ET, including the very low signal-to-noise ratio, missing wedge artifacts from limited tilt angles, and other noise artifacts, collectively hinder the reliable identification and delineation of these structures. In this study, we present ETSAM, a two-stage Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2)-based fine-tuned AI method that effectively segments cell membranes in tomograms. It is trained on a diverse dataset comprising 83 experimental tomograms from the CryoET Data Portal (CDP) database and 28 simulated tomograms generated using PolNet. On an independent test set of 17 experimental tomograms for which ground-truth annotations are available, ETSAM outperforms other deep learning based methods by robustly identifying cell membranes with high sensitivity while also maintaining better precision.

papers.title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model.
papers.authors: Wu X, Zhao Z, Ouyang S, Hao X, Li J, Zhu W, Zhang T, Lu S, Dong T, Jiang N, Yang X, Guo H, Li JP, Tian T, Yang R.
papers.abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response.

papers.title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation.
papers.authors: Kamšek AR, Ruiz-Zepeda F, Tabernik D, Vidergar J, Logar A, Kregar A, Skočaj D, Dražić G, Hodnik N.
papers.abstract: Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

papers.title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage.
papers.authors: Hsieh YC, Konovalov A, Su ZL, Vogel TA, Manohar SG, Apps MAJ, Husain M, Ruff CC, Lockwood PL.
papers.abstract: Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

papers.title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing.
papers.authors: Xu X, Wang X, Cui Y, Liu Q, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo 12 , which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo 12 -based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction.

papers.title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities.
papers.authors: Barnby JM, Dean RJ, Burgess H, Dayan P, Richards LJ.
papers.abstract: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency.

papers.title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields.
papers.authors: He R, Li Y, Chen J, Dinh TM, Stevens CR, Gilchrist AE, Xue Y.
papers.abstract: Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μm thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

papers.title: Histone H3.3 subvariant H3mm15 is required for normal spermatogenesis by regulating gene expression.
papers.authors: Wu Q, Harada A, Ho CH, Tanida E, Tanaka K, Maehara K, Wang B, Shimada R, Ishiguro KI, Ehara H, Sekine SI, Oki S, Ito Y, Kurumizaka H, Takemoto T, Ohkawa Y.
papers.abstract: Histone H3 variants play a fundamental role in chromatin regulation, contributing to gene expression. While the functional diversity of H3.3 subvariants remains largely unexplored, we identified H3mm15 as a testis-expressed H3.3 subvariant that regulates meiotic transcription. Using RNA sequencing and variant-specific reverse-transcription quantitative PCR, we demonstrate here that H3mm15 is expressed predominantly in the testis. Loss of H3mm15 leads to seminiferous tubule disorganization and altered expression of spermatogenesis-related genes. Chromatin profiling reveals that H3mm15 is relatively enriched at promoter-proximal regions compared with H3.3, despite its lower overall chromatin incorporation and lower nucleosomal stability. Functional assays show that H3mm15 has a more moderate impact on transcriptional responses to stimuli than H3.3. Although H3mm15 forms a less stable nucleosome, its reduced stability does not confer enhanced transcription by RNAPII in vitro. Our findings suggest the existence of an H3.3 sub-barcode mechanism, in which structurally distinct H3.3 subvariants differentially regulate chromatin states and contribute to gene regulation during spermatogenesis.

papers.title: Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.
papers.authors: Bora N, Badonyi M, Pathak AK, Manisekaran RG, SG10K_Health Consortium, Marsh JA, Ngeow J.
papers.abstract: Background Many commonly used computational tools for variant effect prediction exhibit ancestry-related bias because they are trained on clinical or population datasets that under-represent global diversity, leading to uneven and sometimes unfair variant classification across ancestries. Multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) and population-free variant effect predictors (VEPs) instead offer alternatives that are unbiased with respect to human ancestry, providing classification evidence that generalises across populations. Methods Here, we evaluate MAVE- and VEP-based classification across five cancer-associated genes with high-quality MAVE datasets, focusing primarily on three leading population-free VEPs: GEMME, EVE, and CPT-1. Results We find that MAVEs are more conservative and decisive in classification, assigning fewer variants to the pathogenic category while yielding fewer indeterminate classifications when calibrated to ACMG/AMP guidelines. Although MAVEs show heightened sensitivity in functionally assayed regions, VEPs identify a broader range of pathogenic variants overall. By combining clinical evidence strengths from MAVEs and VEPs, we reclassify over 90% of variants of uncertain significance across the SG10K_Health and Mexico City Prospective Study reference datasets as at least likely benign or likely pathogenic. We further isolate variants where MAVE- and VEP-based classifications are discordant, highlighting method-specific limitations. Conclusions Together, these findings clarify the complementary strengths of experimental and computational classification approaches and provide a path to less biased and more equitable variant interpretation in clinical genomics, helping to mitigate disparities in diagnosis across ancestries.

papers.title: Attentive interpretable tabular learning (TabNet) for miRNA expression classification in cervical cancer and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Haznedar H, Özsert Yiğit G, Haznedar B.
papers.abstract: Background and objective The classification of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data presents a fundamental challenge in computational biomedicine: raw read counts are high-dimensional, over-dispersed, and heteroscedastic, requiring careful preprocessing before machine learning models can be applied. Existing deep learning approaches for RNA-seq classification have largely overlooked the tabular nature of genomic expression data and have offered limited embedded interpretability. This study proposes TabNet, an attentive interpretable tabular learning architecture, as a framework for miRNA-based disease classification and evaluates its performance and interpretability against three established baseline models. Methods Two publicly available miRNA expression datasets were examined: a cervical cancer cohort (58 samples, 714 miRNAs) and an Alzheimer's disease cohort (70 samples, 503 miRNAs). Raw count data were preprocessed following the MLSeq framework, encompassing DESeq median-ratio normalisation, near-zero variance filtering, supervised gene ranking based on DESeq differential expression analysis, and the DESeq variance-stabilising transformation (vst). Gene subsets corresponding to 5%, 10%, and 30% of the post-filtering feature space were evaluated. TabNet was benchmarked against eight baselines spanning four learning paradigms: a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest, ElasticNet-regularised logistic regression, a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), the prior-fitted transformer TabPFN, and the inherently interpretable Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM). Each configuration was assessed over 50 independent random train/test splits (70%/30%) under a strict leakage-free protocol in which all preprocessing, hyperparameter selection, and early stopping relied exclusively on inner validation subsets of the training partitions; all metrics are reported as mean ± SD. Results Under the leakage-free protocol, a group of four methods reached a statistically indistinguishable accuracy ceiling: on the cervical cancer dataset, ElasticNet (95.06% ± 4.66), EBM (94.94% ± 4.60), TabPFN (94.71% ± 4.64), and Random Forest (94.35% ± 5.82); on the Alzheimer's disease dataset, TabPFN (70.86% ± 10.26), EBM (70.67% ± 12.67), and ElasticNet (70.48% ± 9.76) led. TabNet reached 85.18% ± 11.10 (cervical) and 64.38% ± 11.23 (Alzheimer's) at its respective best levels -- below the top tier, but with the distinctive property of producing sparse, instance-level attention explanations as part of its forward computation. Supplementary analyses showed that self-supervised pre-training conferred no significant benefit at these cohort sizes, that results were robust to the choice between supervised differential-expression and unsupervised variance feature ranking, and that instance-level attention patterns varied substantially across splits, supporting their use as illustrative rather than confirmatory evidence. Conclusions In rigorously leakage-controlled small-cohort miRNA classification, strongly regularised classical models, glass-box additive models, and prior-fitted transformers converge to the same accuracy ceiling, and no evaluated method -- including attention-based deep learning -- surpasses it. Within this landscape, TabNet remains distinctive as the only evaluated deep architecture whose sequential attention mechanism produces sparse instance-level miRNA attributions as an inherent part of prediction, offering a trade-off between embedded interpretability and a moderate accuracy cost that we quantify precisely. These results argue for protocol-first evaluation and calibrated claims when deep tabular models are applied to small transcriptomic cohorts.

papers.title: Photocluster catalytic oxidation enabled by structurally precise copper-hydride nanoclusters.
papers.authors: Yang X, Fang C, Wang Z, Huo R, Wang Y, Li Q, Li S, Shirai T, Xin Y, Sun X, Shen H, Zheng N.
papers.abstract: The utilization of light energy emerges as a prominent strategy to boost nanocluster catalysis, spurring rapid growth in the field termed photocluster catalysis. In particular, structurally well-defined copper-hydride nanoclusters attract attention as promising photocluster catalysts for organic synthesis. Herein, we report Cu 13 H 6 exhibits excellent activity for photocatalytic α-C-H oxidation, revealing great potential in oxidation chemistry. Cu 13 H 6 is one-pot synthesized and characterized using advanced analytical techniques. Critically, machine learning tentatively identifies hydride positions, reducing dependence on neutron diffraction. The Cu 13 H 6 nanocluster exhibits outstanding activity in the photooxidation of diverse alkyl aromatics and alcohols to ketones under mild conditions. This pathway also supports photocatalytic defluorination, deuteriation, cyclopropane ring-opening and dehydrogenative coupling. This work tentatively determines the structure of Cu 13 H 6 using robust stochastic surface walking global optimization with neural network, and identifies the cluster as a versatile, efficient photocatalyst that broadens photocatalysis applications in organic synthesis.

papers.title: Single-cell atlas of fetal immunity across lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood in nonhuman primates.
papers.authors: Doratt BM, Wagner SB, Keen KE, Avila U, Varlamov O, Messaoudi I.
papers.abstract: The fetal immune system develops within a tightly regulated environment that balances immune tolerance with readiness for postnatal antigen exposure. However, limited fetal tissue access constrains understanding of immune ontogeny across compartments. Here we present a multi-tissue single-cell transcriptional atlas of the late-gestation (GD130-135) rhesus macaque fetal immune system, profiling leukocytes from lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood (UCBMC) spanning myeloid, lymphoid, innate lymphoid, and hematopoietic stem cell lineages. Fetal lung is enriched in myeloid cells and ILC2s and shows a proinflammatory bias. Spleen is dominated by T and B cells, with B cells showing enhanced signatures of V(D)J recombination and isotype switching and CD4 T cells showing increased activation and Treg frequency. UCBMC is predominantly composed of T cells with a regulatory transcriptional landscape. Spectral flow cytometry and functional assays corroborate these tissue-specific differences revealing elevated secretion of inflammatory mediators in fetal lung at rest, while spleen and UCBMC show greater inducible responses following stimulation. Together, these data provide a comprehensive cross-tissue atlas of late-gestation primate fetal immunity, revealing tissue-specific immune specialization, functional capacity, and intercellular communication networks that shape immune readiness prior to birth.

papers.title: Consecutive waves of NODAL inhibition are required for epiblast patterning.
papers.authors: Wang M, Hou TJ, Villagrana J, Kijima Y, Dias N, Altus R, Brueckner M, Aktaş T, Sumigray K, Kretzmer H, Smith ZD.
papers.abstract: The mouse genome encodes two Lefty genes that antagonize NODAL signaling to break symmetry during gastrulation. Despite their central regulatory role, accurately describing and comparing their embryonic function remains unclear. Here, we generated high replicate powered single-cell transcriptional atlases of Lefty1 and Lefty2 mutant embryogenesis to evaluate the effects of perturbed NODAL signaling during gastrulation. We find that both mutants exhibit phenotypes beginning with the earliest primitive streak derivatives, suggesting a sequential shift from anterior Lefty1 to posterior Lefty2-based control that prevents spurious differentiation into extraembryonic and axial mesoendoderm at the cost of embryonic mesoderm and, in the case of Lefty1, rostral forebrain specification. By phasing bulk SMAD2/3 ChIP-seq data into single-cell-resolved descriptions of signal transduction, we identify distinct NODAL-responsive modules that track the context-specific use of this morphogen over gastrulation time. Collectively, our work highlights the potential of single-cell assays to decode how complex differentiation processes resolve morphogen signals in space and time.

papers.title: Emergence of polarization in networks of large language model agents.
papers.authors: Piao J, Lu Z, Gao C, Xu F, Hu Q, Santos FP, Li Y, Evans J.
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) have empowered autonomous agents to generate social networks, communicate, and form shared and diverging opinions on political issues. However, our understanding of their collective behaviours and underlying mechanisms remains incomplete. In this paper, we simulate networked systems involving thousands of LLM agents across different backbone models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, ChatGLM, Llama-3, and DeepSeek-V3), in which agents interact through LLM-guided conversations and update their opinions over time, resulting in the emergence of opinion polarization. We discover that these agents spontaneously develop their own social network with properties characteristic of human social networks, such as homophilic clustering. The collective opinions of these LLM agents evolve in ways that exhibit behavioural patterns consistent with social phenomena and mechanisms widely discussed in empirical studies of human behaviour and opinion-dynamics models. This consistency suggests that LLM agents can serve as a valuable synthetic testbed for exploring hypothetical intervention strategies in networked LLM-agent systems. Using this testbed, we further examine the effects of a range of network- and individual-level interventions, such as promoting more diverse interactions and reducing confirmation bias. Overall, this work not only sheds light on subtle opinion dynamics and collective behaviour of LLM agents from a network perspective, but also demonstrates their potential for testing hypotheses about opinion dynamics and intervention strategies.

papers.title: Notch/NF-κB crosstalk signaling controls SASP gene expression during brain aging.
papers.authors: Yang Q, Zarrin H, Hein T, Yildiz B, Prex V, Siontas K, Borggrefe T, Giaimo BD, Friedrich T, Schmitz ML, Wirth T, Oswald F, Baumann B.
papers.abstract: Brain aging is associated with chronic, low-grade inflammation known as inflammaging, which is largely driven by senescent glial cells secreting pro-inflammatory factors termed as senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). In humans, the release of SASP factors in the brain is linked with an increased risk for the development of neurodegenerative disorders; thus, elucidating the underlying molecular mechanisms is essential for understanding the pathophysiology of brain aging. Both NF-κB and Notch signaling are known to regulate SASP expression; however, their mode of interaction in brain inflammaging is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that brain aging is broadly associated with NF-κB activation but Notch suppression using different transgenic mouse models. Astrocytic NF-κB activation in young mice was able to mimic premature SASP formation but repressed Notch signaling in parallel. Bioinformatic analyses further identified conserved crosstalk sites within SASP genes co-occupied by Notch/RBPJ and NF-κB transcription factors in vivo, allowing specific combinatorial regulation. Importantly, selective physical interactions enable that activated Notch can act as a negative modulator of NF-κB signaling at different molecular levels. Consistently, pharmacological activation of Notch in primary astrocytes significantly reduced NF-κB-driven SASP gene expression. Together, these findings identify Notch-NF-κB crosstalk as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate brain inflammaging.

papers.title: New pathogenic ZNHIT3 variants causing fetal hydrops and lethality disrupt snoRNP assembly.
papers.authors: Rahman ML, Bonnard AA, Ruaud L, Guimiot F, Defer I, Wang F, Marchand V, Motorin Y, Yao B, Drunat S, Ghalei H.
papers.abstract: ZNHIT3 is a conserved assembly factor required for biogenesis of box C/D small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein (snoRNP) complexes, which are key players in ribosome biogenesis. Pathogenic variants in ZNHIT3 cause Progressive Encephalopathy with Edema, Hypsarrhythmia, and Optic Atrophy (PEHO) syndrome, a severe neurodevelopmental disorder typically recognized postnatally. Here, we describe two fetuses from a single family who developed isolated hydrops in the early second trimester of pregnancy, resulting in intrauterine demise. Whole-genome quartet sequencing identified two new ZNHIT3 variants, c.40T > C; p.(Cys14Arg) and c.251_254del; p.(Glu84Alafs*8), inherited from healthy parents that present as compound heterozygous alleles in both fetuses. Functional studies using a ZNHIT3 knockdown-rescue system in HEK293T cells demonstrated impaired proliferation and increased apoptosis and revealed distinct molecular consequences for the two variants. One variant produced a stable ZNHIT3 protein lacking the region required for interaction with NUFIP1 and efficient box C/D snoRNP assembly, whereas the second variant reduced ZNHIT3 protein abundance. Both variants impaired snoRNP assembly, reduced the abundance of select box C/D snoRNAs, and caused site-specific losses of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) 2'-O-methylation. These defects were accompanied by changes in ribosome biogenesis and reduced translational output. Together, our findings expand the phenotypic spectrum associated with ZNHIT3 deficiency to include severe antenatal disease and demonstrate that impaired box C/D snoRNP assembly and rRNA modification represent convergent molecular consequences of pathogenic ZNHIT3 variants.

papers.title: Transcription factor CCTF1 plays an important role in regulating proteasome activity during archaeal cell division.
papers.authors: Yang Y, Geng Z, Liang S, Li H, Zhou F, Liu J, Krupovic M, Shen Y.
papers.abstract: Archaea of the order Sulfolobales exhibit a highly ordered cell cycle progression similar to that of eukaryotes. It has been demonstrated that degradation of the cell division protein CdvB by the proteasome controls the progression of cell division. However, how the proteasome itself is regulated during the cell cycle is not fully understood. Recently, the cyclically expressed ArsR (arsenical resistance operon repressor) family transcription factor CCTF1 (cell cycle transcription factor 1) was shown to repress expression of PAN (proteasome-activating nucleotidase) in Sulfolobus acidocaldarius. Here, using biochemical approaches, comparative transcriptomics, and proteomics, we provide further insights into the CCTF1 function and show that it regulates PAN expression in Saccharolobus islandicus by binding to an AT-rich palindromic sequence within the pan promoter. We also reassessed the role of the cyclically expressed protein kinase aCcrK in the regulation of proteasome activity and conclude that CCTF1, rather than aCcrK, is the primary factor controlling the proteasome activity. These findings advance our understanding of the proteasome-mediated cell cycle regulation in archaea.

papers.title: Tracing the spread of Germanic languages using ancient genomics.
papers.authors: McColl H, Kroonen G, Moreno-Mayar JV, Seersholm FV, Scorrano G, Pinotti T, Vimala T, Sindbæk SM, Ethelberg P, Fyfe R, Gaillard MJ, Larsen HME, Mortensen MF, Demeter F, Jørkov MLS, Bergerbrant S, Damgaard PB, Allentoft ME, Vinner L, Gaunitz C, Ramsøe A, Altinkaya I, Henriksen RA, Irving-Pease EK, Sjögren KG, Sabatini S, Fischer A, Barrie W, Ingason A, Rosengren A, Vaughn A, Cao J, Staring J, Stenderup J, Yediay FE, Ahlström T, Akhvlediani I, Albris SL, Aslanishvili V, Atabiev B, Balanovskaya EV, Balanovsky O, Bangsgaard P, Belcastro MG, Card N, Charlier P, Chernykh E, Christiansen TT, Coppa A, De Coster M, Denham SD, Desenne S, Downes J, Frei KM, Gábor O, Gadiev UB, Gårdsvoll JZ, Glørstad ZT, Hansen J, Heeren S, Henriksen M, Heyd V, Høj M, Holst MK, Jankauskas R, Janson H, Jessen MD, Johannsen JW, Johansen T, Kastholm OT, Kern A, Khaskhanov R, Kjær KI, Kolosov V, Kootker LM, Kyselicová K, Larsen AC, Lejars T, Løvschal M, Lynnerup N, Magnusson Y, Malashev VY, Mannermaa K, Masyakin V, Melheim AL, Merkyte I, Moiseyev V, Møller SB, Molnár E, Mortensen N, Murphy E, Nielsen BH, Ödman C, Pany-Kucera D, Schulz Paulsson B, Plets G, Ponce de León MS, Reiersen H, Reinhard W, Sajantila A, Skar B, Slavchev V, Smrčka V, Sørensen L, Tiefengraber G, Uldum OC, Vandkilde H, Vega J, Vitali D, Voloshinov A, Wåhlin S, Wendling H, Wessman A, Wilhelmson H, Wiltschke K, Zilhão J, Zollikofer CP, Korneliussen TS, Chaume B, Demoule JP, Werge T, Olsen L, Nielsen R, Hedeager L, Kristiansen K, Sikora M, Willerslev E.
papers.abstract: Germanic languages, including German, English, Frisian, Dutch and the Nordic languages, are widely spoken across northwest Europe. However, the timing and location of the prehistoric arrival of this Indo-European linguistic phylum, as well as its Iron Age diversification, remain contentious 1-3 . Here, by sequencing 712 ancient human genomes and analysing them alongside 4,009 previously published genomes, we identify an archaeologically elusive population that entered Sweden, likely from the Baltic region, by around 4000 BP. This population, which became widespread throughout Scandinavia by 3500 BP, offers a potential vector for the introduction of the Germanic language group to Scandinavia 4-6 , some 800 years later than traditionally assumed 7-9 . Following the Late Iron Age disintegration of Germanic into its descendant languages, we observe by 1650 BP a southward migration from southern Scandinavia into presumed Celtic-speaking areas, including present-day Germany, Poland and the Netherlands. During the subsequent Migration Period (1575-1375 BP), we see this ancestry among Germanic-speaking Anglo-Saxons in Britain and Langobards in southern Europe. In the same time period, we identify a related large-scale northward back-migration into Denmark and southern Sweden, coinciding with the rise of Danish influence and the linguistically documented emergence of Old Norse. These findings indicate that multiple migrations and geographical locations had a major role in the arrival and formation of Germanic, as well as in its divergence into historical and modern descendant languages.

papers.title: FMT combined with atezolizumab-bevacizumab in hepatocellular carcinoma refractory to immunotherapy: an open label, single-arm, phase II pilot study.
papers.authors: Pomej K, Frick A, Scheiner B, Baumgartner M, Schmetterer KG, Reyna-Blanco CS, Balcar L, Pajancic L, Kreuter A, Séneca J, Hausmann B, Köcher T, Prinzensteiner M, Lampichler K, Rohr-Udilova N, Chakrabarty A, Klotz A, Lampl AC, Zinober K, Regnat K, Trauner M, Berry D, Tamandl D, Vogl T, Gasche C, Pinter M.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) may help to overcome resistance to immunotherapy. In this single-center, single-arm phase II hypothesis-generating pilot study (FAB-HCC), we included 12 patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who progressed on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab. Patients received a single FMT via colonoscopy from a donor with HCC who responded to anti-PD-1 treatment or a healthy donor, combined with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab. The primary endpoint was safety as measured by incidence and severity of treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Secondary endpoints included radiological response and survival. Grade 3-4 TRAEs included arterial hypertension (n = 5) and proteinuria (n = 3), both related to bevacizumab, and diarrhea (n = 1), related to FMT. No serious TRAEs were observed. Objective response rate was 33% (n = 4/12) and median progression-free survival was 6.9 (95%CI, 3.0-10.8) months. Following FMT, recipient microbiome composition appeared more similar to that of the donor, and healthy donor FMT seemed to be associated with higher engraftment. FMT appeared to be associated with enrichment of response-associated and loss of deleterious gut bacteria. Circulating PD-1 + CD8 + T cells decreased and CD32b + CD14 high CD16 low monocytes increased following FMT plus immunotherapy. Phage-display immunoprecipitation sequencing revealed that antibody repertoire stability, rather than global diversity or composition, changed over time. Taken together, FMT combined with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab was safe and associated with a high response rate in patients with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab-refractory HCC. Given the limited sample size, these findings need cautious interpretation and confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05750030.

papers.title: Reward function compression facilitates goal-dependent reinforcement learning.
papers.authors: Molinaro G, Collins AGE.
papers.abstract: Humans can uniquely assign value to novel, abstract outcomes to support reinforcement learning. However, this flexibility is cognitively costly and reduces learning efficiency. We propose that goal-dependent learning initially relies on capacity-limited working memory. With consistent experience, learners create a compressed reward function - a simplified rule - that transfers to long-term memory for automatic evaluation upon receiving feedback. This automaticity frees working memory resources, thereby boosting learning efficiency. Across six experiments, we demonstrate that learning is impaired by the size of the goal space but improves when this space allows for compression. Additionally, faster reward processing correlates with better learning. Although the algorithmic details remain to be established, computational modeling revealed that individual differences in compression efficiency, proxied by reward processing speed, led to higher choice accuracy. Together, our behavioral results and computational models suggest that efficient goal-directed learning relies on compressing complex goals into stable reward functions.

papers.title: Game theory driven multi-agent framework mitigates language model hallucination.
papers.authors: Liu R, Bie B, Wang Z, Ma Y, Liu Y, Li X, Yang H, Yang W, Cao J, Tao S.
papers.abstract: Lightweight large language models hold promise for scientific applications but remain limited in rule-constrained domains because they can reproduce linguistic patterns without following scientific principles, leading to hallucinations. Here, we show that G-Frame, an adaptive multi-agent framework inspired by Bayesian game and team game principles, enables a closed-loop process for automated data generation, model evaluation, and training. By assigning complementary roles to multiple agents, G-Frame generates structured reasoning data and constructs a specialized corpus containing 363,045 chain-of-thought examples and 199,589 question-answer pairs. Using this corpus together with domain pre-training and adaptive training, the 7-billion-parameter model OmniChem achieves competitive performance across the reported benchmarks and reduces the ChemJudge hallucination rate from 41.95% for the base model to 12.91%. Case studies further illustrate potential applications in molecular design and selected synthesis-planning tasks. These results support G-Frame as an extensible game theory-driven multi-agent framework for improving the reliability of lightweight scientific language models.

papers.title: Sub-stoichiometric degradation is dispensable for potent PROTACs as demonstrated by irreversible covalent BTK degraders.
papers.authors: Cheng R, Lin H, Yu X, Misra S, Mitchell AD, Woyach JA, Qi X, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent a transformative therapeutic modality, yet the viability of covalent PROTACs remains debated, as irreversible binding seemingly contradicts the catalytic mechanism of action. Here, we develop and characterize PSIRC3, a potent covalent PROTAC for Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). PSIRC3 induces selective BTK degradation with a sub-nanomolar DC 50 of 0.75 nM and a D max of 85%, while its non-covalent counterpart is inactive. Such activity requires covalent bond formation with Cys481, as efficacy is abolished against the C481S BTK mutant. PSIRC3 achieves maximum BTK degradation within 30 min, a kinetic profile linked to rapid cell permeation and efficient ternary complex formation. In vivo, a single administration of PSIRC3 leads to substantial BTK degradation in both PBMCs ( > 80%) and splenocytes ( > 50%). Computational modeling, parameterized with our experimental data, reveals that degradation efficacy is governed by a balance between E3 ligase and target affinities: excessively high E3 affinity is detrimental by inducing a hook effect, while higher target affinity is generally beneficial. Our findings provide strong evidence that covalent engagement can drive potent and selective protein degradation, challenging the notion that catalytic turnover is indispensable for PROTAC efficacy, and open avenues for targeting intractable proteins.

papers.title: Estimating the completeness of large-scale single-cell sequencing projects.
papers.authors: Miihkinen M, Chu Y, Vakkilainen S, Akimov Y, Aittokallio T.
papers.abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. Capitalizing on single-cell RNA sequencing, many initiatives and substantial resources are cataloguing these differentiated cell types by their transcriptomic profiles. Despite the extensive efforts to profile various organs and their cellular compositions, we lack metrics to assess the completeness of the sequencing projects. In this cellular biodiversity analysis, we leverage the increasingly available single-cell data together with statistical methods, originally developed for assessing the species richness of ecological communities, to estimate dataset completeness based on current data from single-cell profiling technologies. Deriving from such cellular richness estimates, we establish a practical statistical framework that enables reliable assessment of the completeness of any large-scale single-cell profiling project, after which additional sequencing efforts do not anymore reveal new cellular clusters. Such estimates can serve as stoppage-points for the ongoing sequencing projects, hence guiding a more cost-efficient completion of the profiling of various human tissues.

papers.title: DNA mimic helical foldamers with up to 100 units: synthesis and recognition of a multiprotein complex.
papers.authors: Loos M, Därr F, Douat C, Gourdon-Grünewaldt L, López-Francos A, Brem A, Hopfner KP, Huc I.
papers.abstract: DNA mimic foldamers (DMFOs) are helically folded aromatic oligoamides that mimic the shape and charge distribution of double-stranded B-DNA. DMFOs consist of an alternation of two amino acid monomers, M and Q. Here, we introduce a new synthetic approach of (MQ)n oligomers on solid phase that enabled the production of sequences as long as a 100mer, formally equivalent to a 50-base pair DNA duplex. The approach takes advantage of dimeric Fmoc-MQ-OH as building blocks. Three such macromonomers were synthesized using Q and M units bearing different side chains. Solid phase synthesis protocols were validated in all series. Helix handedness was shown to be determined by a single chiral residue. The purified long oligomers were analyzed by reversed phase HPLC, mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for their purity, identity, and helix-handedness bias. Clusters of foldamers forming in the presence of Ca2+ could be visualized by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM). Lastly, a 72mer DMFO was shown to bind to the A-module of the chromatin remodeling complex INO80 slightly tighter than a comparable DNA duplex. A cryo-EM structure of the complex at a resolution of 3.59 Å showed that the DMFO occupies the A-module DNA binding region.

papers.title: CFDP1 is required for histone variant H2A.Z deposition by the human SRCAP chromatin remodeling complex.
papers.authors: Moro N, Yang D, Butty VL, Levine SS, Peterson CL, Boyer LA, Watanabe S.
papers.abstract: Craniofacial Developmental Protein 1 (CFDP1) is a member of the evolutionarily conserved family of Bucentaur (BCNT) proteins and is required for cell survival and differentiation during tooth development. Its yeast homolog is involved in histone variant H2A.Z deposition by the yeast SWR1C remodeler. Direct connections between CFDP1, H2A.Z deposition, and the mammalian SWR1 homolog, Snf2-Related CREBBP Activator Protein (SRCAP), are poorly understood. Here, we perform detailed biochemical reconstitution and characterization of the human SRCAP complex (SRCAP-C). We find that CFDP1 weakly interacts with SRCAP-C in a salt concentration-dependent manner and is essential for H2A.Z dimer exchange by SRCAP-C. We show that CFDP1 stimulates the basal ATPase activity of reconstituted SRCAP-C, suggesting a requirement for CFDP1 in regulating intrinsic catalytic ATPase activity. Additionally, CFDP1 deficiency in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) leads to a genome-wide reduction of H2A.Z, H3K27me3, and H3K4me3 deposition, accompanied by the upregulation of developmental genes normally marked by these modifications. Taken together, our results provide mechanistic insights into how CFDP1 regulates histone variant H2A.Z deposition by SRCAP-C. Given mutations in the SRCAP gene cause Floating-Harbor syndrome, a rare, dominant developmental disorder, our study provides an additional link between craniofacial development and SRCAP-mediated H2A.Z deposition.

papers.title: Systematic engineering of synthetic minimal promoters for tunable transgene expression in mammalian cells.
papers.authors: Zaitsev-Chaikovsky M, Shalev S, Lanton T, Dalyahu Y, Nissim L.
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning transgene levels is crucial in fundamental and applied research. Native promoters are broadly utilized to regulate transgene expression. However, their large size and structural complexity hinder predictable tuning, constrain compatibility with viral vectors with limited capacity, and increase the risk of homologous recombination. Synthetic promoters are short de novo sequences, typically consisting of an enhancer region, which is positioned upstream of a minimal promoter that determines transcription initiation efficiency. Enhancer optimization typically yields coarse activation shifts, alters response curves, and requires case-by-case optimization. Synthetic minimal promoter architecture enables fine-tuning that is potentially compatible with any enhancer region. In this study, we systematically optimized minimal promoter sequences, core element composition, and regulatory motif sequences. Our findings support a modular model of minimal promoter function in which cis-regulatory elements from different minimal promoters can be mixed, altered, added, or deleted to yield predictable expression outcomes. We shortened and thereby enhanced the efficiency of known minimal promoters, engineered modular tunable minimal promoters, and generated candidate regulatory elements spanning 7-8 nucleotides that drive efficient transcription when combined with artificial ${5^{\prime}}$ untranslated regions (5'UTRs) that function as an additional regulatory layer. This framework broadens the utility of synthetic promoters for next-generation applications.

papers.title: Correction to 'Molecular basis for the regulation of retroviral nucleosomal integration by chromatin compaction'.
Coupling metabolic enhancement to plasmid spread enables programmable antimicrobial control.
papers.authors: Dorado-Morales P, Calvo-Villamañán A, Niedermeier L, Audrain B, Lambérioux M, Ducos-Galand M, Ghigo JM, Stecher B, San Millán Á, Mazel D.
papers.abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant pathogens underscores the need for precise antimicrobial strategies beyond conventional antibiotics. Conjugation-based approaches offer a powerful yet underexploited means of delivering targeted genetic interventions within microbial communities. Here, we combine selective killing modules with optimized conjugative vectors to target antibiotic-resistant pathogens and clinically relevant resistance plasmids. First, we engineered toxin-intein modules, programmable cassettes that restrict toxic activity to specific regulatory contexts. We developed modules targeting Shigella spp., Salmonella enterica, and bacteria carrying the resistance plasmid pOXA-48, demonstrating tunable and selective activity at both species and strain levels. To identify the optimal delivery platform, we compared mobilizable and conjugative plasmids, finding that conjugative systems consistently outperform mobilizable ones by approximately one order of magnitude. We then streamlined the broad-host-range plasmid RP4 and enhanced its functionality by incorporating the metabolic fos locus, a type IV pilus operon or both features combined. Integration of the anti-pOXA-48 module into these vectors enabled effective suppression of resistance plasmid spread in complex microbial communities. Together, these results advance the use of conjugative plasmids as programmable antimicrobial platforms and identify delivery efficiency and ecological competitiveness as key determinants of the success of such interventions.

papers.title: Detection and quantification of DNA double-strand breaks by genomic and imaging methods: a critical appraisal of capabilities and limitations.
papers.authors: Dobrucki J, Rowicka M.
papers.abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are the most genotoxic form of DNA damage. Unrepaired DSBs may cause loss of chromosome fragments at mitosis, while incorrectly repaired DSBs can cause chromosome aberrations and other adverse effects, leading to cell cycle arrest, senescence, cell death, or neoplastic transformation. Detecting and quantifying DSBs is important in studies of genome instability, aging, and cancer. Methods of detecting and quantifying DSBs fall into two broad categories: imaging-based methods, used to detect and localize DNA breaks in individual cells, and genomic methods, a new category utilizing massively parallel DNA sequencing to map DSBs genome-wide in a cell population. Imaging and genomic methods yield fundamentally different information. This review focuses on a critical evaluation of the capabilities and limitations of genomic and imaging methods for the detection and quantification of DSBs. It explains why the class of genomic methods, where quantification is based on counting the detected unique DSBs and the number of cells in the sample, results in inaccurate assessment of the average number of DSBs per cell and how this problem can be solved. We also discuss complementarity of genomic and imaging methods and potential directions of their future development.

papers.title: Correction to 'BRCA2-dependent homologous recombination is required for repair of Arsenite-induced replication lesions in mammalian cells'.
The African swine fever virus I73R protein is a multifunctional Zα domain that mediates both Z-binding-dependent and -independent biological functions through induction of phase separation.
papers.authors: Pirotte S, Liu Y, Conti L, Conti L, Won H, Im SJ, Ferhad C, Hu Y, Donohoe O, Diallo MA, Gong L, Wang R, Kim YG, Chen H, Vanderplasschen A.
papers.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) I73R encodes a protein consisting only of a Zalpha (Zα) domain. Here, we studied its biochemical properties. Complementary approaches demonstrated that I73R is a multifunctional Zα domain that combines Z-binding, B-to-Z conversion, and liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) induction activities. I73R proved to be a better converter than human ADAR1 Zα, and it retained conversion activity with Y48I mutation of its Z-binding site. Next, we investigated I73R biological functions, leading to the following findings: (i) Ectopic expression of I73R or mutated I73R with deficient Z-binding both inhibited arsenite-induced stress granules to a similar extent, and none of these proteins localized within these organelles. (ii) I73R formed cytosolic condensates with dsRNA, Z-DNA, and Z-RNA in ASFV-infected cells. (iii) Rescuing of ASFV I73R deletion by sequences encoding natural, mutated, and chimeric forms of Zα domains demonstrated that I73R mediated both Z-binding-dependent and -independent biological functions through induction of LLPS. This conclusion was further supported by the effect of the LLPS inhibitor 1,6-hexanediol on the replication of ASFV I73R recombinant strains. This study further demonstrates the functional diversity that exists among Zα domains. It unravels new outlooks targeting Zα domain-mediated LLPS for the development of pharmaceutical molecules able to regulate viral and cellular Zα domain-containing proteins.

papers.title: Varied Ensembles of Long-range ChROmatin interactions drive chromatin compartmentalization.
papers.authors: Ostwal Y, Muzzopappa F, Heurteau A, Raffel R, Veluchamy A, Eswara K, Boudellioua A, Ali S, Kumari R, Depierre D, Vadlamani S, Schickele N, Schaak S, Erdel F, Cuvier O, Fischle W.
papers.abstract: The chromatin components that are involved in organizing eukaryotic genomes into active and inactive compartments remain unclear. In analysing viable Caenorhabditis elegans mutants lacking different chromatin-regulatory proteins, we found that the HP1-type factor HPL-2 and the MBT-domain protein LIN-61 jointly contribute to chromatin compartmentalization. Genomic regions bound by both proteins and their cognate histone mark H3 lysine 9 dimethylation (H3K9me2) form broad interfaces of 30-50 kilobases that engage in combinatorial interactions, which we term 'Varied Ensembles of Long-range ChROmatin interactions' (VELCROs). Remarkably, VELCROs are defined by high density of H3K9me2, HPL-2, and LIN-61 sites, but not by the intensity of their individual peaks. Mutants that display defective chromatin compartmentalization are impaired in VELCROs. Polymer simulations show that VELCROs can drive a phase transition that segregates B from A chromatin compartments depending on peak densities. Our work identifies VELCROs as stochastic ensembles of interactions constrained within defined chromatin hubs that shape genome compartmentalization.

papers.title: Correction to 'New targets and procedures for validating the valence geometry of nucleic acid structures'.
Monomeric ZRANB3 drives replication fork reversal.
